articles.title: Incêndio em Caapiranga: moradores arriscam a vida contra o fogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo teria começado no sábado (29) e segue neste domingo (30). Moradores também questionam falta de assistência do poder público para combater as chamas.
articles.summary: O incêndio em Caapiranga atinge a Estrada do Membeca e moradores denunciam a falta de apoio das autoridades para conter as chamas que ameaçam sítios da região.
articles.body:
Um forte incêndio atingiu uma área de vegetação localizada na estrada do Membeca, em Caapiranga , no interior do Amazonas. O fogo teria começado no sábado (29) e segue neste domingo (30). Segundo moradores, há temor de que as chamas cheguem a sítios na região.

Vídeos publicados nas redes sociais mostram a dimensão do incêndio que vem se espalhando pela mata às margens da estrada ( assista acima ). Imagens obtidas pela Rede Amazônica revelam que ao menos três pacas morreram carbonizadas.

Até a atualização mais recente desta reportagem, não há informação sobre feridos, nem sobre as causas do incêndio.

Em outra gravação, um morador da região reclama da falta de assistência do poder público.

"Desde ontem nós estamos pra morrer aqui e não aparece um vereador, um prefeito [...] e o povo se acabando aqui de fogo. Não mandam um carro com 100 litros d'água."

Segundo ele, desde que o incêndio começou, apenas os moradores se mobilizaram para tentar conter o fogo.

"Está acabando os sítios tudinho. 'Nós' tudo morrendo e não tem uma pessoa pra dar assistência. É a gente arriscando a vida pra não queimar o que nós estamos há mais de dez anos ai cuidando".

O g1 questionou o posicionamento do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM) sobre o incêndio em Caapiranga, mas até a atualização mais recente desta reportagem não obteve resposta.

articles.title: Ciclista é assaltado em rua do Jardim Oceania, em João Pessoa; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens mostram momento em que vítima é obrigada a deitar em calçada, no Jardim Oceania, em João Pessoa.
articles.summary: Imagens mostram momento em que vítima é obrigada a deitar em calçada, no Jardim Oceania, em João Pessoa.
articles.body:
Um ciclista foi assaltado na manhã deste domingo (30), no bairro Jardim Oceania, em João Pessoa . O crime ocorreu na Rua Professora Maria Jacy Pinto.

Nas imagens, é possível ver o momento em que o homem, que estava de bicicleta, é obrigado a deitar na calçada. Em seguida, um dos suspeitos revista os bolsos da vítima.

Após a abordagem, o assaltante sobe na garupa de uma moto, que é guiada por um segundo homem, e a dupla foge do local.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a vítima e os suspeitos não haviam sido identificados. Também não há informações sobre o que foi levado.

Assalto aconteceu no bairro Jardim Oceania, em João Pessoa — Foto: Reprodução/TV Cabo Branco

articles.title: Mãe salva filha de atropelamento e é atingida por moto no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmera de segurança registrou o momento em que mulher corre para retirar criança da pista em Floresta do Araguaia. Menina não ficou ferida.
articles.summary: Mãe salva filha de atropelamento em Floresta do Araguaia após criança invadir a pista; câmera de segurança registrou o impacto da moto contra a mulher.
articles.body:
Uma mulher foi atingida por uma motocicleta ao correr para retirar a filha da pista e evitar que a criança fosse atropelada, em Floresta do Araguaia , no sul do Pará. O acidente ocorreu na quarta-feira (26) e foi registrado por uma câmera de segurança.

As imagens mostram a menina deixando a calçada e caminhando em direção à avenida. Ao perceber a aproximação da criança da área de circulação dos veículos, a mãe corre para alcançá-la.

Durante a tentativa de retirar a filha da pista, a mulher é atingida de frente por uma motocicleta que trafegava pela via. Com o impacto, ela e o motociclista caem no asfalto.

A menina consegue se afastar e não é atingida.

Pessoas que estavam próximas ao local prestaram ajuda à mãe e ao motociclista após o acidente.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informações oficiais sobre o estado de saúde dos dois envolvidos.

articles.body:

Além disso, 13 jogos ocorreram em casas lotéricas físicas e seis foram feitos por canais eletrônicos.

O prêmio para as apostas que acertarem as seis dezenas era de R$ 29.343.361,52. No entanto, nenhuma aposta marcou a sena e o prêmio do próximo sorteio está estimado em R$ 36 milhões.

Confira apostas ganhadoras da Mega-Sena 3051 em Sergipe

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

Mega-Sena bilhete volante Loterias — Foto: Millena Sartori/g1

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

articles.title: Dia vira noite após tarde abafada, e SP tem chuva e vento forte | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências (CGE) da Prefeitura de São Paulo, os termômetros chegaram aos 31°C neste domingo, enquanto a umidade relativa do ar ficou em torno de 50%.
articles.summary: De acordo com o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências (CGE) da Prefeitura de São Paulo, os termômetros chegaram aos 31°C neste domingo, enquanto a umidade relativa do ar ficou em torno de 50%.
articles.body:
Tempo fecha em SP neste domimgo — Foto: Rodrigo Rodrigues/g1

A tarde deste domingo (30) foi de sol entre nuvens, calor e tempo abafado na Grande São Paulo. Mas o cenário mudou: a chegada de áreas de instabilidade aumentou a quantidade de nuvens e provocou pancadas de chuva, com raios e rajadas de vento que podem superar os 50 km/h.

Às 15h05, a Defesa Civil emitiu alerta severo para região de Embu, Zona Oeste e Sul da capital, com previsão de raios, vento e condição para granizo. Pouco depois, o alerta foi emitido para a Zona Leste e região do ABC Paulista.

De acordo com o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências (CGE) da Prefeitura de São Paulo, os termômetros chegaram aos 31°C neste domingo, enquanto a umidade relativa do ar ficou em torno de 50%.

O tempo abafado e a chegada de áreas de instabilidade vindas da região de Sorocaba favoreceram a formação de mais nuvens e provocaram pancadas de chuva. Em alguns pontos, a chuva pode ser mais forte e acompanhada de raios e ventos acima dos 50 km/h.

Com isso, aumenta o risco de alagamentos que podem atrapalhar a passagem de veículos e pedestres e de queda de árvores. Às 15h10, a Zona Sul, Oeste e Centro entraram em estado de atenção para alagamentos.

Depois da chuva, semáforos da Avenida Santo Amaro, na Zona Sul, ficaram apagados.

Agosto acumulou, até o momento, 27,9 mm de chuva na capital. O volume corresponde a aproximadamente 93,9% dos 29,7 mm esperados para o mês.

Alerta da Defesa Civil neste domingo (30) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Na segunda-feira (31), o tempo continua abafado, com sol entre nuvens. As temperaturas devem ficar entre 19°C e 32°C, podendo passar dos 32°C. A umidade do ar pode chegar a valores próximos de 35%.

No fim da tarde, a quantidade de nuvens aumenta e há previsão de chuvas rápidas e isoladas.

Na terça-feira (1º), o dia ainda começa com sol entre nuvens e tempo abafado. A chegada de uma frente fria, porém, deve mudar o tempo ao longo do dia.

As primeiras pancadas de chuva podem ocorrer ainda pela manhã. À tarde, a chuva deve ganhar força e variar de moderada a forte intensidade, acompanhada de raios e rajadas de vento que podem superar os 50 km/h.

A previsão também indica aumento do risco de alagamentos e queda de árvores.

As temperaturas devem cair, com mínima de 17°C e máxima de 25°C. A umidade relativa do ar deve ficar acima de 70%.

A frente fria avança pelo litoral paulista no início de setembro e deve provocar chuva, ventos fortes e queda nas temperaturas.

articles.title: Ciro Gomes estuda câmeras em fardas de policiais no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato do PSDB iniciou sua agenda de campanha neste domingo (30) em um adesivaço no cruzamento das Avenidas Washington Soares e Oliveira Paiva.
articles.summary: Em campanha em Fortaleza, Ciro Gomes propõe câmeras em fardas de policiais e novo serviço de inteligência para reforçar a segurança pública no Ceará.
articles.body:
Ciro participa de adesivaço em Fortaleza. — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/Sistema Verdes Mares

O candidato ao governo do Ceará, Ciro Gomes (PSDB) , iniciou sua agenda de campanha neste domingo (30) em um adesivaço no cruzamento das Avenidas Washington Soares e Oliveira Paiva, em Fortaleza .

Na ocasião, ele falou sobre suas propostas para a segurança pública do estado e criticou a maneira como o governador Elmano de Freitas, candidato à reeleição pelo PT, vem conduzindo o combate às facções criminosas.

Ciro disse que estuda a incorporação de câmeras corporais em fardas de agentes de segurança do estado. Em fala anterior, ele havia dito ser contra o uso dos equipamentos, mas afirmou ter conversado com sua equipe e passou a estudar a ideia.

"Me apressei, dei uma resposta pouco reflexiva, minha equipe me chamou a atenção imediatamente e eu vou rever, já estou revendo essa questão. Não é que eu decidi por colocar, mas eu lhe explico porque eu me apressei. É porque hoje a grande tarefa nossa na direção de cessar a impunidade é motivar o aparelho policial do Ceará (...) Então, refraseando, estamos em estudo a questão das câmeras", informou.

No discurso, ele também propôs a construção de um novo serviço de inteligência para o Ceará, com duas camadas.

"A primeira camada é a inteligência comunitária. Cada líder comunitário, cada vereador, cada pessoa do interior sabe exatamente quem são os faccionados, a cadeia de comando, quem é que está dando a ordem, quem é que está fornecendo a arma, mas não falam. Por quê? Porque não tem segurança nenhuma, nem proteção nenhuma".

Ciro informou que pretende garantir proteção para as vítimas e testemunhas e também propôs a contratação de mil agentes de segurança, que serão treinados nas "escolas mais sofisticadas de inteligência do mundo".

"Eu já estou conversando com dignitários estrangeiros, embaixadores, ou para levar os chefes nossos aqui para treinar no estrangeiro, ou ir para trazer instrutores do estrangeiro para nos equipar com as melhores ferramentas de segurança pública. A partir daí, com comandos específicos, cirúrgicos, nós vamos retirar essa cadeia de comando de circulação, com a linguagem que for necessária. Esta é a única forma de se enfrentar crime organizado", explicou o candidato.

A agenda de Ciro deste domingo (30) ainda inclui a inauguração de um comitê da candidata a deputada federal Dayanna Colaço em Beberibe.

articles.title: O diretor de escola que salvou 900 estudantes das inundações no Nepal | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Se tivéssemos tomado essa decisão 10 minutos mais tarde, nenhum de nós — nem eu, nem os alunos — estaria aqui hoje', relata o diretor da escola à BBC
articles.summary: 'Se tivéssemos tomado essa decisão 10 minutos mais tarde, nenhum de nós — nem eu, nem os alunos — estaria aqui hoje', relata o diretor da escola à BBC
articles.body:
O diretor de escola de ensino médio, Rajendra Dawadi que salvou estudantes no Nepal — Foto: BBC

O diretor de uma escola nepalesa devastada pelas enchentes afirma que decidiu evacuar cerca de 900 alunos para um local seguro após receber uma série de telefonemas que alertavam para o risco de inundação na região.

Rajendra Dawadi, diretor da Escola de Ensino Médio Tribhuvan Trishuli, em Nuwakot, no Nepal — que conta com um total de pouco mais de 1.600 alunos —, relata ter recebido quatro avisos de pessoas diferentes em um intervalo de poucos minutos.

Entre esses avisos, havia relatos de que as águas da enchente já haviam atingido o povoado de Betrawati, situado rio acima.

"Decidi que não deveria mais esperar. Mesmo que a enchente não chegasse, tratava-se apenas de um dia de aula", relata ele à BBC.

Enquanto evacuavam os alunos para um local mais elevado, Dawadi viu o prédio de um alojamento, situado a cerca de 100 metros do rio, ser tomado pelas águas.

"Se tivéssemos tomado essa decisão 10 minutos mais tarde, nenhum de nós — nem eu, nem os alunos — estaria aqui hoje."

Uma das 900 estudantes salvas pela decisão do diretor foi Yunisha, de 16 anos, que conta ter escapado momentos antes da inundação.

"Eu e meus amigos escapamos por uma diferença de apenas 10 segundos", diz ela à BBC.

Yunisha descreve como correu por um caminho estreito e lamacento atrás da escola junto com outros alunos.

"Em pouquíssimo tempo, o mercado foi levado pela água diante dos meus olhos", acrescenta ela.

Yunisha, que foi entrevistada ao lado de sua mãe, Sabina Shrestha, conta que a família passou horas tentando desesperadamente entrar em contato com ela após saber da inundação.

A jovem Yunisha, de 16 anos (ao centro), diz ter escapado por uma questão de 10 segundos — Foto: BBC

"Eu estava em pânico. Tentei ligar várias vezes para minha filha e para o pai dela, mas não consegui falar com nenhum dos dois", detalha a mãe.

Quando finalmente conseguiu contato, Shrestha lembra-se de sentir certo alívio.

Mas a família continuou angustiada até que Yunisha voltasse para casa — três dias depois.

"Estou tão feliz e aliviada. Deus salvou minha filha", celebra Shrestha.

A inundação ocorrida na quarta-feira (26/8) matou pelo menos 794 pessoas e mais de 2,5 mil estão desaparecidas no Nepal, dizem autoridades locais

No Tibete, o número oficial de mortos é de 16, com 546 desaparecidos, segundo a mídia estatal chinesa.

As equipes de resgate estão trabalhando para encontrar sobreviventes.

Além da população local, há informações de cidadãos desaparecidos de Índia, China Estados Unidos, Ucrânia, Malásia, Austrália, Reino Unido, Canadá, Coreia do Sul, África do Sul, Portugal, Holanda e Nova Zelândia.

Segunda enchente pode ter sérios impactos mesmo que seja menor que a primeira, alerta especialista

Um especialista em inundações alerta que a preocupação imediata no Nepal e no Tibete é que as enchentes repentinas criem novos problemas.

Jeff Da Costa, pesquisador em sistemas de alerta precoce de inundações e risco de desastres na Universidade de Reading, no Reino Unido, explica que os detritos do desastre bloquearam rios e formaram novos lagos.

Da mesma forma, a infraestrutura da região está gravemente danificada, o que significa que "uma segunda inundação não precisa ser tão grande quanto a primeira para causar impactos graves", afirma ele.

Da Costa diz que monitorar as mudanças nos lagos e nas barreiras da região, bem como rastrear onde eles podem romper, "é agora de extrema importância".

O pesquisador acrescenta que é importante que a China e o Nepal compartilhem informações de monitoramento, pois "o que acontece num lugar pode afetar rapidamente as pessoas do outro lado da fronteira".

"As informações precisam circular com a mesma rapidez e levar a decisões práticas no local", acrescenta.

Da Costa também descreve como as mudanças climáticas constituem um contexto fundamental para o desastre, uma vez que o aquecimento está alterando as geleiras, o permafrost (o solo que fica constantemente congelado) e a estabilidade das encostas em toda a região do Himalaia.

No entanto, ele ressalta que o desastre não pode ser atribuído às mudanças climáticas sem uma análise mais aprofundada.

articles.title: Chuva em Promissão destelha estádio e causa queda de energia | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura informou que não há registro de desalojados. Telhado da arquibancada e do vestiário do Estádio Municipal foram levados com a força do vento.
articles.summary: Após chuva em Promissão destelhar o estádio municipal e causar alagamentos, equipes trabalham para restabelecer a energia e realizar o rescaldo dos danos.
articles.body:
Uma chuva forte acompanhada de rajadas de vento causou queda de energia e pontos de alagamento em Promissão (SP), na manhã deste domingo (30). Não há registro de feridos ou desalojados.

Segundo a prefeitura, o Estádio Municipal "Verano Piromalli" foi a estrutura mais atingida da cidade. A cobertura da arquibancada do local e o telhado do vestiário caíram com a força do vento e, com isso, parte dos danos atingiram a rede elétrica do estádio. Assista acima.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil Estadual, as rajadas de vento chegaram a 50km/h na cidade. A cobertura da quadra da escola "Professora Aurélia Moreira de Barros" também foi levada devido à força do vento.

Estádio ficou danificado devido à chuva — Foto: Vanderlei dos Santos

Além disso, foram registrados pontos de alagamento nos bairros Jardim São João e Jardim do Lago. A rede de energia elétrica foi afetada nas regiões.

Em nota, a a Companhia Paulista de Força e Luz (CPFL) informou que a energia já foi restabelecida para a maioria dos clientes afetados. As equipes da distribuidora seguem atuando nos casos até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A prefeitura ainda afirma que os trabalhos de rescaldo devem continuar até a segunda-feira (31). A orientação é que os moradores evitem áreas alagadas e não se aproximem de árvores que apresentem riscos de queda, ou de fios de energia caídos ou danificados.

articles.standfirst: Nenhuma aposta acertou as seis dezenas, e o prêmio acumulou em R$ 36 milhões. O próximo sorteio será realizado na terça-feira (1º).
articles.summary: Nenhuma aposta acertou as seis dezenas, e o prêmio acumulou em R$ 36 milhões. O próximo sorteio será realizado na terça-feira (1º).
articles.body:
Duas apostas do Paraná acertaram cinco números da Mega-Sena no concurso 3051, sorteado na manhã deste domingo (30).

Uma das apostas foi feita em Guarapuava e levou R$ 55.635,04 .

A outra foi registrada em Bandeirantes e ganhou R$ 111.270,08 . Apesar de as duas terem acertado cinco números, os valores dos prêmios são diferentes por causa da quantidade de números apostados. Entenda abaixo.

🍀 As dezenas sorteadas foram: 11 - 15 - 20 - 21 - 38 - 48.

Nenhuma aposta acertou as seis dezenas, e o prêmio acumulou em R$ 36 milhões. O próximo sorteio será realizado na terça-feira (1º).

📦 Por que a aposta de sete números ganhou mais?

Na Mega-Sena, o apostador pode marcar de 6 a 20 números. Quanto mais dezenas escolher, maior é o valor da aposta e também aumentam as chances de ganhar.

Quem faz uma aposta com sete números participa, na prática, de sete combinações diferentes de seis dezenas. Por isso, quando acerta cinco números, recebe um prêmio maior do que uma aposta simples de seis números.

Bilhetes da Mega-Sena — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

A Mega-Sena tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, às quintas e aos domingos.

📶 É possível apostar em qualquer lotérica do país ou pela internet, no internet banking da Caixa Econômica Federal ou no site ou app das Loterias Caixa , que podem ser acessados por celular, computador ou outros dispositivos.

🔞 Para concorrer, é necessário ter mais que 18 anos de idade.

💰A aposta mínima, de 6 números, custa R$ 6. Quanto mais números marcar, maior o preço da aposta e mais chances de faturar.

articles.title: Henrique canta com fã mirim e inspira internautas: 'Inesquecível' | G1
articles.standfirst: Sertanejo cantou para o pequeno Rhyan Cristal, que é cadeirante, e dedicou música à mãe do garoto. Registro repercutiu na web.
articles.summary: Sertanejo cantou para o pequeno Rhyan Cristal, que é cadeirante, e dedicou música à mãe do garoto; registro repercutiu na web.
articles.body:
O cantor sertanejo Henrique, da dupla com Juliano, emocionou internautas ao protagonizar um momento de carinho e atenção com um fã mirim. Em um vídeo que circula nas redes sociais, o artista aparece em cima de uma motocicleta cantando diretamente para o pequeno Rhyan Cristal, que é cadeirante e acompanhou a apresentação do ídolo com admiração.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Ao cantar junto com o garoto, Henrique atendeu a um pedido de Rhyan e interpretou uma música em homenagem à mãe do menino, tornando a ocasião ainda mais marcante. Nas redes sociais, a mãe de Rhyan publicou o registro e agradeceu ao cantor pelo acolhimento.

"Como é bom ser fã de um ídolo que, além de talentoso, é humano. Henrique foi superatencioso com Rhyan, cantou com ele e tornou esse momento inesquecível", escreveu.

Canção com a criança repercutiu nas redes sociais — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Rhyan Cristal & família

O encontro com o garoto aconteceu nos bastidores do show da dupla no Parque de Eventos Zezé Rocha, em Lagarto (SE), realizado no último sábado (29). De acordo com informações publicadas no site oficial dos cantores, a apresentação foi a atração principal da 63ª Vaquejada de Lagarto.

Além de cantar no palco que também recebeu artistas como Henry Freitas, Bia Frazzo e Patrick Costa, Henrique participou da vaquejada montando e correndo na pista de competições do local.

articles.title: Rohingya crisis: Aid falls and hope fades
articles.summary: UNHCR’s Bangladesh representative, Ivo Freisen, warns that dwindling aid is driving hope down among Rohingya refugees.
articles.body:
Nine years after the mass exodus of Rohingya refugees from Myanmar, more than one million stateless people remain in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar. The crisis is becoming increasingly difficult to sustain as humanitarian funding declines; refugee numbers grow and living conditions deteriorate.

In this discussion, UNHCR representative in Bangladesh, Ivo Freisen, says hope is fading as desperation grows, with about 95 percent of mainly Muslim Rohingya refugees relying fully or largely on humanitarian assistance. He warns that limited education and opportunities are pushing some young Rohingya to risk dangerous sea journeys in search of a better life.

Freijsen says a lasting solution depends on creating conditions for a safe, voluntary and sustainable return to Myanmar, including addressing discrimination, citizenship and freedom of movement.

articles.title: Piers Morgan helps groom get helicopter from wedding to Lord's
articles.summary: Peter Melhuish, from Guildford, is playing at Lord's less than 24 hours after his wedding in Wales.
articles.body:
Piers Morgan has donated £1,000 to help a groom get a helicopter so he can play at Lord's immediately after his wedding in North Wales.

Peter Melhuish, from Guildford in Surrey, is playing at Lord's on 6 September for Blackheath in the final of the Cawston Press Village Cup, but his wedding is less than 24 hours before.

A fundraiser was set up for the team captain and along with his donation, Morgan said: "As someone who also comes from Guildford and has also always dreamed of playing in the village cup final at Lord's, I'm very glad you will now be living my dream. Good luck Peter!"

Melhuish said he and his wife-to-be were "absolutely amazed and touched by the support".

He added: "I can't promise anyone runs or wickets on the Sunday. However, I can promise that if we make it to the ground and I'm able to play at Lord's, you will have helped make a young cricketer's dream of playing for Blackheath in a national final at Lord's come true."

Melhuish, who has been at the club since he was six, says regardless of the result, "I'll already have won when I marry Izzy".

The pair planned the wedding for the Saturday after Blackheath's local league fixtures finished for the season.

But they did not factor in the club's success in the Village Cup, a nationwide tournament played on Sundays by local teams across the UK.

Melhuish said if it was not for the one-hour flight, he would have to take a taxi at 05:00 instead "which wouldn't be much fun".

On the fundraising page, which received more than £6,000, it said there had been donations from club members, sponsors, other local clubs, and teams they had played in the cup en route to the final.

Any surplus funds will be donated to UK-based charity Kids for Kids, which supports children in Darfur in Sudan.

articles.title: After renaming ‘Gulf of Mexico’ to ‘Gulf of America’, Google Maps changes name of ‘Lake Ontario’ for users in the US
articles.summary: Tech News News: Google Maps has officially changed its display label for Lake Ontario to “Lake America” for users inside the US, implementing the adjustment in respon.
articles.body: Google Maps has officially changed its display label for Lake Ontario to “Lake America” for users inside the US, implementing the adjustment in response to a presidential executive order issued late last week. The change mirrors a similar geographic revision enacted in February 2025, when Google Maps altered the designation of the Gulf of Mexico to “Gulf of America.”In an official blog post, Google explained that the updated naming convention appears differently depending on where the user is browsing from around the world.The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States. Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S., people using Maps in the U.S. will see "Lake America," those in Canada will continue to see "Lake Ontario," and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names. These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now.Canada defends historical originsAccording to a report by 9to5google, Canadian officials confirmed that their national cartography and official records will retain the historic title without alteration. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney emphasised the centuries-old heritage behind the original phrasing.“The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America. It comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means ‘the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.’”Meanwhile, competing service MapQuest reportedly stated that it will not adopt the change, rolling out an interactive custom name generator designed to let users invent alternative titles for the lake. Apple Maps has not yet applied the updated wording, though the company previously mirrored Google’s shift to “Gulf of America” within two days during the February 2025 revision.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Chicago mass shooting leaves 1 dead, 9 injured Saturday night
articles.summary: Chicago police are investigating a mass shooting on the city’s South Side, with one person dead and at least nine others injured.
articles.body: Chicago police are investigating a mass shooting on the city’s South Side, with one person dead and at least nine others injured. According to Chicago police, officers were attempting to disperse a large crowd on the 5400 block of South Cottage Grove Avenue just after 11:30 p.m. when gunfire rang out. Police say at least 10 individuals were hit by gunfire in the shooting, which occurred in the city’s Washington Park neighborhood. One of the victims, a 35-year-old man, was shot multiple times, and was pronounced dead at the scene according to the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office. Six victims who were shot were rushed to area hospitals and were listed in good condition, according to police. Police are working to obtain information on three other victims, including a 37-year-old woman, a 23-year-old woman and a 35-year-old man. All three were taken to area hospitals, but their conditions are unknown at this time. No Chicago police officers were hit by gunfire during the attack, according to authorities. No suspects are in custody, and Area One detectives are investigating.

articles.title: ‘Gift from Venezuela’: Donald Trump says oil deal will help refill ‘virtually emptied’ US strategic reserve
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said oil secured under a recently announced deal with Venezuela would be used to replenish the Strategic Petroleum.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said oil secured under a recently announced deal with Venezuela would be used to replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), which has been drawn down sharply in recent years amid global supply disruptions and high fuel prices.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the process of refilling the reserve would begin shortly, describing the Venezuelan oil as a “Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States.”“One of the things I am going to do with the Venezuelan Oil is fill up the Strategic National Reserves which, because of Sleepy Joe Biden, has been virtually emptied,” Trump wrote.“The ‘topping out’ process will begin very shortly, and is a Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States”, he added.SPR near a 44-year lowThe Strategic Petroleum Reserve held about 290 million barrels of oil as of August 21, near a 44-year low, according to Reuters.The stockpile was drawn down under both the Biden and Trump administrations in response to global supply disruptions, including Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the conflict with Iran.It remains unclear how quickly the Venezuela deal could supply oil to the reserve or provide any near-term benefit to US motorists.Trump announced the agreement with Venezuela on Friday as part of efforts to revive the South American country's battered oil industry.However, significant investment and infrastructure work would be required before Venezuelan production can rise substantially.What is known about the Venezuela dealThe US government and an unnamed private operator in Venezuela have formed a new company that has been granted rights to untapped oil fields for 100 years.A statement from Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez said the agreement involves the development of 17 fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels.Also read: What we know about Trump’s ‘biggest oil deal in world history’She said the deal could attract $100 billion in investment into Venezuela's oil industry and generate more than $209 billion in taxes for Caracas.According to a US official cited by news agency AP, the United States will receive 55% of the new company's effective output, including an ownership stake and rights to buy oil at cost.Oil purchased by the US would go towards the Strategic Petroleum Reserve as well as the military.However, several key details remain unclear, including the identity of the private operator, who will fund the required infrastructure investments and how the US stake in the company will be structured.Will the deal lower US fuel prices?The agreement is not expected to deliver an immediate increase in Venezuelan oil production.Experts believe that Venezuela's ageing and damaged oil infrastructure would require years and billions of dollars in investment to repair.“It’s going to take time — many years — to deploy that much capital and produce the kind of incremental results that history suggests possible,” Kevin Book, managing director at ClearView Energy Partners, told AP.The average price of petrol in the US stood at about $4.08 a gallon on Saturday, compared with $3.20 at the same time last year, according to AAA data.Trump has said the Venezuela agreement will help lower fuel prices for Americans, but the immediate impact remains unclear as the country's oil sector would need substantial investment before production can increase significantly.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Tropical Storm Karina strengthens into a hurricane in the Pacific, could be a major storm this week
articles.summary: Tropical Storm Karina strengthened into a hurricane in the Pacific Ocean on Sunday and could become a major storm this week, forecasters said.
articles.body: MIAMI — Tropical Storm Karina strengthened into a hurricane in the Pacific Ocean on Sunday and could become a major storm this week, forecasters said. The cyclone’s center was at far out sea and was not threatening land. Karina had maximum sustained winds of 80 miles per hour (130 kilometers per hour), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center said, making it a Category 1 hurricane. A major hurricane is Category 3 or greater. The storm was located about 820 miles (1,325 kilometers) southwest of the southern tip of Mexico’s Baja California Peninsula and was moving and was moving northwest at 15 miles per hour (24 kilometers per hour) a forecast path farther out into the Pacific. While Karina was expected to stay well away from land, swells from the storm were likely to cause dangerous surf and rip current conditions along parts of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula, the hurricane center said. Elsewhere in the Pacific, Tropical Storm Lowell was 1,150 miles (1,850 kilometers) southeast of Hawaii, and it too posed no threat to land. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has forecast a below-average Atlantic hurricane season due to El Nino. It predicted eight to 14 named storms, with three to six of them reaching hurricane strength and one to three intensifying to major hurricanes.

articles.title: In the 1940s, Bing Crosby bought Nevada ranches to escape Hollywood; one 3,000-acre property that could run 600 cattle has now sold for $14.2 million, nearly twice its 2019 asking price
articles.summary: News News: In the 1940s, at the height of his fame as a singer and movie star, Bing Crosby sought refuge from Hollywood by buying a string of ranches in northeas.
articles.body: In the 1940s, at the height of his fame as a singer and movie star, Bing Crosby sought refuge from Hollywood by buying a string of ranches in northeastern Nevada. One of those properties, which was a roughly 3,000-acre working cattle ranch in Elko County, has just sold off-market for $14.2 million, according to The Wall Street Journal (WSJ). The sale price is about double the ranch’s original pre-pandemic asking price of $7.28 million when it first hit the market in 2019. The deal underscores how demand for large, well-watered Western ranches has surged in recent years, even as the property’s Hollywood pedigree adds a layer of historic allure.A Hollywood escape in the high desertCrosby, best known for hits like 'White Christmas' and his Oscar-winning role in 'Going My Way', owned seven ranches in the Elko area during the 1940s and 1950s. He was a frequent summer visitor to the region and was even named honorary mayor of Elko in 1948, a testament to how deeply he embedded himself in the local community.Like many celebrities of his era, Crosby used remote Western properties as a counterpoint to the pressures of studio life. The open ranges, quiet towns and rugged landscape of northeastern Nevada offered a stark contrast to Los Angeles and the constant attention that came with stardom. The ranch that just sold was part of that larger retreat—a place where he could ride, hunt and simply step away from the spotlight.From working cattle operation to luxury ranch assetThe 3,000-acre property is a fully functional cattle ranch capable of running about 600 head, according to reporting on the sale. It includes a five-bedroom, 5,000-square-foot house, a private airstrip and an airplane hangar—amenities that appeal to both ranchers and high-net-worth buyers looking for a remote getaway with easy access.The seller, Jim Boyer, is a Nevada-based retired telecom entrepreneur who previously told the Journal he was selling because he wanted a break from the work of operating the ranch. He started shopping the property about four months ago, after pulling it from the market during the pandemic, according to listing agent Todd Renfrew of Outdoor Properties of Nevada, as per the report.Why the price nearly doubled since 2019When the ranch first listed in 2019, the asking price was $7.28 million. It was taken off the market during the pandemic and then quietly re-marketed earlier this year without a publicly advertised price. The final $14.2 million sale—nearly twice the original ask, reflects broader shifts in the Western land market over the past several years.Renfrew told the Journal that the market for large land properties surged during the pandemic, and irrigated grounds have continued to appreciate. The ranch’s value increased significantly because of its substantial water resources, while surrounding regions have become less affordable, he said. In other words, a well-watered, turnkey cattle operation in a relatively accessible part of the West is now a much scarcer—and more valuable—commodity than it was in 2019.A historic name in a changing marketCrosby’s name still carries weight in real estate, especially for properties tied to his personal history. The singer also owned homes in Palm Springs, Palm Desert and a now-famous estate in Hillsborough, California, which sold for $25 million in 2025 and has since been relisted at nearly $29 million after renovations.In Nevada, however, the ranch’s appeal is less about Hollywood glamour and more about its combination of history, working infrastructure and natural resources. For some buyers, the Crosby connection is a compelling story; for others, the key factors are the acreage, water rights and ability to run cattle at scale.The listing agent declined to name the buyer, but the off-market nature of the deal suggests a private purchaser rather than a institutional investor.What the sale says about Western ranch landThe Bing Crosby ranch sale fits into a larger pattern of rising prices for large Western properties, especially those with reliable water and established agricultural use. As coastal and urban real estate becomes more expensive and volatile, some buyers are shifting capital into land that offers both lifestyle value and tangible assets: grazing capacity, irrigation, mineral rights and recreation.At the same time, properties with a historical narrative, whether tied to a celebrity, a pioneering family or a particular industry, can command a premium over comparable land without that story. In this case, Crosby’s ownership adds a layer of cultural history to a property that already checks the boxes for serious ranch buyers.A quiet chapter closes in Elko CountyFor Elko, a small city about 420 miles north of Las Vegas, Crosby’s legacy is part of local lore. His honourary mayoralty, frequent visits and ownership of multiple ranches helped put the area on the map for outsiders, even as it remained a working cattle and mining community.With this sale, one of the last major Crosby-linked ranches in the region changes hands under very different market conditions than those of the 1940s, or even 2019. The new owners will inherit not just a productive cattle operation and a substantial land base, but also a piece of mid-century Hollywood history tucked into the high desert of northeastern Nevada.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Son realizes missing American dad was in path of Nepal disaster after watching viral video
articles.summary: Sunny Patel saw viral flood footage from Nepal and Tibet and realized his father, Jitendra Patel, was in that exact area on a spiritual pilgrimage.
articles.body: A family is searching for answers after an American traveling on a spiritual pilgrimage went missing amid a catastrophic Himalayan flood that has left hundreds dead and thousands unaccounted for. Sunny Patel was watching viral footage of the torrent on the border between Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region when he realized his father, Jitendra Patel, could have been caught in the disaster. TRAPPED NEPALI WORKERS PULLED FROM HYDROPOWER TUNNEL AFTER CATASTROPHIC FLOODING "I watched the video and I just thought of how horrific it was. And then... probably 30 seconds later, it registered," he recalled. "I texted my mom, and she was hoping that we hadn't seen the video. But of course, it was so viral by then... My mom responded and said, 'That's exactly where he was,' actually." Sunny said he had last spoken to his father on Wednesday morning around local time, when he believed his father had already crossed the border from Nepal into China, though he has been unable to confirm the details. The most frustrating part, he said, is the lack of information coming out of China. He added that his family has spoken to embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing, as well as the U.S. State Department. DEATH TOLL FROM MUDSLIDES, FLOODING AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER CLIMBS PAST 670; NEARLY 3,000 MISSING They have filed missing person reports "with every agency we can think of, and some have been responsive." "We're trying to go on these media segments and get the awareness out there that there are people on the Chinese side that we aren't getting a ton of information about." Experts believe Wednesday's mudslides and flash flooding across Nepal and Tibet were caused by a large chunk of ice breaking off a glacier and falling into the Lhende Khola River, which sent stories-high waves of rock, ice and debris hurtling through the mountain river systems. Newly released figures say more than 600 people have been killed so far and more than 3,000 remain missing, with over 4,000 rescued so far. AMERICAN CLIMBER'S REMAINS FOUND AFTER AVALANCHE IN PAKISTAN, OTHER MOUNTAINEERS STILL MISSING That morning, Jitendra was with a group heading up to Mount Kailash — a place where thousands of people go every year on a spiritual pilgrimage, according to Sunny. "They were actually supposed to be there the day prior and unfortunately had some car troubles from what we can make out... which, you know, of course, could be all the difference." Sunny said his dad "believed in the goodness of everybody, probably to a fault," and "lived with kindness in his heart." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "He always, always, always said, 'God is good...' If you called him and said, 'How you doing?' He would say, 'I'm the best, God is great.' And he was just the most upbeat, positive person I've ever met." Search and rescue operations were temporarily suspended on Saturday because of rain and heavy fog. Authorities are also monitoring two lakes upstream formed by the disaster, one of which was overflowing at times.

articles.title: Third murder charge over stabbing of teen at Brent Civic Centre
articles.summary: David Wynter, 17, died after he was attacked on Engineers Way near Brent Civic Centre.
articles.body:
A total of three people have now been charged with murder over the fatal stabbing of a 17-year-old boy at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley.

David Wynter died after he was attacked on Engineers Way at about 14:30 BST on 25 August.

A 15-year-old boy was charged with murder two days later, and two more teenagers - a 17-year-old boy and 18-year-old Jahquarn St Hillaire - were charged with murder and possession of an offensive weapon on Saturday.

The 15-year-old was remanded in custody and is due to appear at the Old Bailey on 24 September, with the other pair due at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Monday.

A 20-year-old man, Diego Farquharson, of Birchen Grove, Brent, has been charged with assisting an offender and is due to appear before magistrates on Monday.

Wynter's family continue to be supported by the force, the Metropolitan Police said.

Police said their investigation was ongoing and urged anyone with information or footage to come forward.

Extra patrols have been deployed in the area following the stabbing.

articles.title: Face scans are replacing passports at U.S. airports. Here's who can — and can't — opt out.
articles.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection is rolling out facial recognition at every U.S. airport. Here's who can opt out — and who has to submit.
articles.body:
"IDs out, please." You've heard it at every U.S. airport after an international flight for as long as you've been flying. Soon, you may not. Get ready to be camera-ready when you get off an international flight.

In an interview with the Washington Examiner published this week , Diane Sabatino, CBP's executive assistant commissioner for field operations, described a future of international travel that does not include reaching for a piece of plastic in your pocket. In some cities, she said, it's already here.

"In a few years … people with Global Entry are going to be walking through at all of our airports, unless a CBP officer wants to speak to that traveler," Sabatino told the Examiner.

Facial recognition for arriving international passengers is available at 238 U.S. airports . A faster version for U.S. citizens, called Enhanced Passenger Processing, is in 33. A third program, Seamless Border Entry, clears pre-approved Global Entry members through in under three seconds at seven airports without the traveler stopping at all.

Whether you have a choice depends on your citizenship.

Yes. American citizens can still ask for a manual check by a CBP officer. Anyone using an EPP kiosk who doesn't want their photo taken can alert an officer and be changed to the regular line, according to CBP.

Sabatino has repeatedly said the process is optional for U.S. citizens.

Not anymore. A federal rule that took effect Dec. 26 requires biometric identity checks for all non-U.S. citizens entering or leaving the country by air, land or sea, Nextgov reported .

That is a change from the previous rule, which exempted children under 17 and adults over 79. Both groups will now have to submit to face scans or fingerprints on arrival and departure.

The photo taken is instantly crosschecked against a government database of existing passport, visa or travel document images, according to CBP . CBP has said the match is more than 98% accurate.

Since June 2017, about 848 million people have gone through the process, per figures Sabatino has cited. More than 529,000 people who overstayed their visas have been identified using the technology.

When does every airport get the fully touchless version?

CBP says it will take three to five years to bring biometric entry and exit to every airport, seaport and land crossing. Some of the newer touchless technology, including the "corridors" that let travelers walk past cameras without stopping, is being tested at Orlando International Airport. Airlines and airports pay for the biometric exit equipment, which is part of why the rollout has been scattered.

A new baggage-screening system that lets CBP officers review checked bags remotely while a flight is still in the air will launch at JFK's new Terminal One in 2027, according to the Washington Examiner report.

Congress ordered a biometric entry-exit system in 1996 and accelerated it after Sept. 11, 2001. It has taken more than two decades to build. Last year's federal budget package added new funding to speed up deployment.

Katrina Poulsen, a visitor from Denmark, stands in front of a face recognition camera after arriving at customs at Orlando International Airport, Thursday, June 21, 2018, in Orlando, Fla. Florida's busiest airport is becoming the first in the nation to require a face scan of passengers on all arriving and departing international flights, including U.S. citizens, according to officials there. articles.title: Nepal begins burials after preserving DNA; only 29 flood victims identified so far
articles.summary: South Asia News: NUWAKOT, NEPAL: Authorities in Nepal began temporarily burying unidentified victims of Bhote Koshi-Trishuli-Naryani flood in shallow graves after coll.
articles.body: NUWAKOT, NEPAL: Authorities in Nepal began temporarily burying unidentified victims of Bhote Koshi-Trishuli-Naryani flood in shallow graves after collecting DNA and forensic evidence as morgues overflowed and remains recovered far downstream became increasingly difficult to identify.An update issued on Sunday evening said only 29 of the 650-plus bodies had been identified even as recoveries continued along the roughly 200km river system.Nepal Police spokesperson DIG Abi Narayan Kafle told TOI that 211 of the first 669 recovered remains were mutilated, partial or severed. “Many remains were buried under thick mud and water for two to three days,” he said. Bodies swept dozens of km from Rasuwa were recovered in Nuwakot, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahun and Nawalparasi, often far from where victims disappeared.Chitwan became the biggest pressure point. By Sunday, 259 bodies had been recovered along Trishuli and Narayani riverbanks there but only nine identified. Authorities began moving unidentified remains to Devghat forest after post-mortem examination and DNA collection, with 26 placed underground in the first batch.The process was designed so burial does not end a family’s search for closure -- every body was assigned an identification number; photographs, physical features, clothes, jewellery and other belongings were recorded, while DNA, fingerprints and other forensic samples were preserved. Burial locations were geo-tagged so remains could later be located and exhumed if relatives established identity.“If family members come forward in the future to claim a missing relative, these scientific and legal records will allow us to confirm identity and locate the exact burial plot,” Kafle said.Gorkha district also buried 29 unidentified bodies and body parts after collecting DNA. “Gorkha does not have sufficient mortuary facilities, and bodies are being recovered every day,” chief district officer Tulsi Prasad Shrestha said. Nawalparasi East began a similar process on Sunday, placing 20 unidentified remains underground after forensic sampling and assigning identification numbers.For families, identification increasingly depended on small personal details. More than 1,000 relatives reached Pokhara on Saturday to examine photographs of 102 bodies brought from downstream districts. Police said families recognised loved ones through tattoos, necklaces, earrings and even school uniforms.One father from Bidur identified his five-year-old son, whose body had been recovered far downstream in Nawalparasi, after seeing a photograph online. The clues were the child’s school tie, necklace and earring.“Where faces are no longer recognisable, relatives are identifying bodies through other things on their person,” police inspector Deepak Rijal said. “More relatives are continuing to arrive.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 5 years after withdrawal, a grave picture for Afghans inside and outside the US
articles.summary: The fifth anniversary of the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan falls as the nation’s citizens face a starkly different picture than when they first arrived in America, with the Trump administration employing numerous tactics to deport Afghans and halt the arrival of new refugees. Since President Trump returned to office, he has drastically curtailed the pathways…
articles.body:
The fifth anniversary of the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan falls as the nation’s citizens face a starkly different picture than when they first arrived in America, with the Trump administration employing numerous tactics to deport Afghans and halt the arrival of new refugees.

Since President Trump returned to office, he has drastically curtailed the pathways for Afghans to arrive in the U.S., even curbing immigration processing for several countries following a fatal attack on National Guardsmen carried out by an Afghan national.

Under the second Trump administration, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has moved to strip temporary protected status (TPS) for Afghans, ending protections that kept more than 8,000 people from being deported. The administration has also begun the process of reviewing and revoking some special immigrant visas (SIVs) given to Afghans who worked alongside the U.S. in military and government efforts as interpreters, special operations partners and local embassy staff.

And the White House as one of its earliest moves also suspended refugee processing except for white South Africans, cutting off hopes of many Afghans of reaching the U.S.

“As we take stock of whether the U.S. has lived up to its obligations and promises to the Afghans who worked and served alongside American military personnel and partners, often at great personal risk, the answer is a resounding no,” Sharif Aly, president of the International Refugee Assistance Project said on a recent call with reporters.

“The Trump administration has closed virtually all pathways for Afghans to receive visas or enter the U.S., even as there are over 5 million Afghans currently displaced all over the world.”

For Afghans and their advocates — a group that includes many veterans who served in the country — things have gone from bad to worse.

Twenty years of U.S. involvement in the county came to an end over two weeks of chaos at Hamid Karzai International Airport, with throngs of people crowded outside in the hopes of being boarded onto a limited number of flights slated to take allies to safety. More than 80,000 were evacuated through Operation Allies Welcome.

Despite the two decades of nation-building, the Taliban now control the country, and women — who had been free to attend school and pursue careers — are now shut off from most aspects of public life.

And Afghans who did make it to the U.S. live in a precarious state. Even those who gained an SIV or who have a green card have received letters warning them the basis for that status has been revoked .

“Five years ago, this was a crisis. Everything was on fire, nobody had a plan, and the failures were failures of capacity. That is not what this is anymore,” Shawn VanDiver, president and founder of #AfghanEvac, told reporters.

“Today it is not a crisis. It is a deliberate choice, grounded in policy this government has not had the courage to verbalize or brief.”

The Trump administration has shut off virtually every possible pathway for Afghans to reach the U.S. while taking a number of steps to enable deportations of those currently here.

Afghanistan is among the countries on Trump’s travel ban, which bars citizens from a number of countries from getting tourist visas. A second expanded travel ban stripped the narrow exceptions that had allowed for processing of Afghan SIVs, effectively ending the program.

Afghanistan was also on the list of 75 countries for which Trump suspended immigration visas, also cutting off routes for those seeking to join family in the U.S. While a judge last weekend vacated the policy , the State Department on Tuesday paused immigrant visa appointments worldwide to carry out “in-depth training” for consular officers, arguing they need to screen out foreign applicants at risk of taking advantage of U.S. public assistance.

And for those within the U.S., their standing is shakier than ever.

Getting an SIV is a lengthy process, one that requires “chief of mission” approval, in which high-ranking State Department officials sign off on an applicant’s proof of employment. But the Trump administration has been reviewing the basis for those SIVs — a process that began under former President Biden, but which NPR found has been escalating under Trump .

Many who came to the U.S. on the evacuation flights also may not qualify for an SIV, which required two years of qualifying work. Some who were evacuated did not meet that threshold, forcing them to apply for asylum, a lengthy process with no certain outcome.

For all those with tenuous statuses, TPS was the protection blocking them from being deported. The Trump administration has ended TPS for 13 out of 17 total countries, with the remaining four set to expire shortly.

“People who went through the steps to secure it really felt like it was a backstop for them,” Joseph Azam, board chair of the Afghan-American Foundation, told The Hill.

“And so, with that being gone, I think people feel like they’re walking a tightrope without a net, and that’s really scary.”

Laila Ayub, co-founder of the Afghan Network for Advocacy and Resources, said she and other immigration attorneys donating their time frequently have to deliver bad news.

“We find ourselves facing difficult conversations every day, explaining to our clients and our friends and family that there is little that we can do as attorneys,” she said on a call with reporters.

Ayub said while some lawsuits have paused or limited some Trump administration plans, that hasn’t really made a difference on the ground.

“There’s little that we can do when they’re facing, for example, delays with their green cards or asylum, and even less that we can do to help them reunite with their families without action from Congress and others,” she added.

“Every time that there’s a bit of good news — which we’re so grateful for the lawyers who are challenging many of these policies — we end up having a conversation where people in our community think this means that there’s now a pathway back open for their family to come here, and the reality is that that’s still not the case.”

Some Afghans are already being deported.

VanDiver this week highlighted the case of one man, a 24-year-old known in court documents as K.Y., applying for asylum where an immigration judge granted them a withholding of removal to Afghanistan, determining he would be likely to face persecution there.

While in the past, such a determination meant someone would not be deported, the Trump administration has taken to removing migrants to third countries. This man is now facing removal to the Central African Republic, where the State Department warns that armed groups control much of the country and conflict breaks out regularly.

Inside Afghanistan, Azam said, people are losing hope, both of fleeing to the U.S. or adjusting to the new reality of life under the Taliban.

“The people who I hear from that are most distressed and most kind of lacking in hope are still Afghan women,” Azam said, “especially when you know a lot of the public narrative in support of them is waning.”

He called it “a generational setback” as “the path Afghanistan’s on because of this policy is very different than what it was on five years ago where half its population now is erased from public life, erased from education, erased from certain careers, and also erased from the political discourse.”

There are also still many Afghans stuck in limbo across the globe — those who were able to flee to the country but unable to reach the U.S.

Some were ferried out on official flights or other privately arranged charters, while others escaped on their own.

“There are still about 260,000 Afghans stuck in roughly 90 countries — Afghanistan, Pakistan, Qatar and so many more, waiting on a promise the United States made to them,” VanDiver said.

“And many Afghans who did make it here, including the ones our own government put on planes and flew to this country, are being harassed by ICE,” VanDiver continued, referring to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). “That’s the story. Both halves of it. Stuck out there and hunted in here.”

Numerous legislative efforts to aid Afghans in the U.S. and abroad have stalled over the years, including a sweeping effort — the Afghan Adjustment Act — that would provide a pathway to citizenship for all Afghans who arrived under the Biden administration, triggering a fresh round of vetting. It would also smooth processing of Afghans who would qualify as refugees.

Under the Trump administration, the legislative vehicles have narrowed, focusing instead on seeking to protect TPS for Afghans, as well as shore up the SIV program.

Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.), a veteran who served in Afghanistan, is one of the co-sponsors of a bill that would protect TPS for Afghans through 2029.

“We had a good inflow of refugees from Afghanistan, and then this current administration pretty much shut it off. I think it’s wrong. We have a moral obligation to those we served with in Afghanistan, who served by our side, helping us out. We had a promise, and a promise made should be promises kept, absolutely,” Bacon said on a call with reporters.

He said he believed the bill could advance under a discharge petition to force a vote given that there is some GOP support, but he said that TPS should be a “fallback plan” until Congress could gain support for a bill to give that same population a pathway to citizenship.

“I think that the appropriate, the humanitarian, the merciful, the right policy is to find a pathway towards permanent status and citizenship down the road for people in this category — particularly Afghan TPS — is what we should be trying to do,” he said.

But action to do so seems further away than ever.

“All the work we did, like sleeping on the Capitol steps, all this energy and momentum, and all these different ways we tried to crack this nut for almost five years,” Azam said, “it wasn’t enough then, and it’s really not enough now.”

articles.title: Tropical Storm Karina strengthens into a hurricane in the Pacific, could be a major storm this week
articles.summary: US News: MIAMI: Tropical Storm Karina strengthened into a hurricane in the Pacific Ocean on Sunday and could become a major storm this week, forecasters said. .
articles.body: MIAMI: Tropical Storm Karina strengthened into a hurricane in the Pacific Ocean on Sunday and could become a major storm this week, forecasters said. The cyclone's center was at far out sea and was not threatening land.Karina had maximum sustained winds of 80 miles per hour (130 kilometers per hour), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center said, making it a Category 1 hurricane. articles.title: College football player dies after collapsing on sidelines moments after scoring touchdown
articles.summary: A running back for William Jewell College in Missouri died Saturday after suffering a medical emergency during the first quarter of his team’s season opener, shortly after scoring a touchdown.
articles.body: A running back for William Jewell College in Missouri died Saturday after suffering a medical emergency during the first quarter of his team’s season opener, shortly after scoring a touchdown. MicahJo Barnett, a junior business administration major at the Division II school, had a health crisis on the sidelines following the score, according to a statement released by the college. The home game against Fort Lewis College at Greene Stadium in Liberty, Missouri, was canceled after the incident. Neither William Jewell athletics nor the NCAA, which also released a statement on Barnett’s death, disclosed the nature of his medical emergency. Barnett was a Liberty native who played at Liberty North High School, where he helped lead the team to a state championship in 2023, according to records. “Micah’s life was taken far too soon, leaving his family, friends, teammates, and community heartbroken,” read a message on a GoFundMe page set up for his family by one of his former youth coaches. The post described Barnett as “a talented and kind young man who was loved by so many.”

articles.title: Educated? Skilled? Ambitious? Traffickers are looking for you
articles.summary: Young jobseekers are being recruited into scam compounds. Urgent action is needed to disrupt these trafficking schemes.
articles.body:
Good salary. Visa sponsored. Flight included. Applicants must be educated, fluent in English and confident online.

It sounds like a great opportunity for a young graduate, but it is the bait in a trafficking operation.

The advertised job does not exist. On arrival, the person’s passport is taken. They are moved to a compound they cannot leave and are forced to run online scams: impersonating strangers, building false relationships and persuading people thousands of kilometres away to send money.

Those who miss their targets may be beaten, starved or placed in solitary confinement. Their families may sell land or take on debt to raise money to pay for their release.

I heard versions of this story firsthand during a recent visit to Rwanda, where I met two survivors who had been trafficked through fraudulent job offers. They were fluent in English and comfortable with technology. They had been looking for the same thing as millions of other young people: a good job and the chance to build a better future.

Those qualities made them valuable to the traffickers. They were given scripts and forced to impersonate women online, build romantic relationships with people in Europe and persuade them to send money.

Today, after returning home with support from the International Organization for Migration (IOM), they are working alongside us to warn communities and other young people. They are using some of the same platforms on which traffickers search for recruits to help others recognise the danger.

Their experience exposes a crime that creates victims on both sides of the screen. One person is held under threat and forced to deceive. Another has their trust exploited and may lose their savings. The criminal network profits from both.

At least 300,000 people are estimated to have been trafficked or coerced into scam compounds across Southeast Asia. People from at least 80 countries and territories have been identified among them.

Across the Asia Pacific, scams cost people an estimated $88bn to $114bn in 2025. Those losses cover a wider range of scams, but they show the scale of the criminal economy in which these compounds operate.

The threat is also reaching further into Africa. IOM and its government partners are identifying a growing number of victims from countries like Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. During recent visits to Tanzania and Rwanda, leaders told me of fraudulent job offers reaching young graduates and other jobseekers through social media.

These networks are global by design. Recruitment may happen in one country, travel through another and exploitation in a third. The scams can target people anywhere. When an operation is disrupted, it moves and starts again elsewhere.

Government responses are often divided. Labour authorities see an unlicensed recruiter. Border officials see suspicious travel. Police see online fraud. Consular teams see citizens stranded abroad. Traffickers exploit the gaps between them.

These gaps need to be closed. Governments should provide trusted ways to verify overseas employers, recruiters, contracts and visas. Labour, border, police and consular authorities need to share alerts quickly and investigate the networks together.

Technology companies have an equally important role. Fraudulent recruitment happens openly on social media, messaging services and job platforms. Companies should detect and remove deceptive advertisements, make them easy to report and preserve evidence that can help identify those responsible. Awareness campaigns designed with survivors must reach young people in those same spaces.

Above all, people forced to run scams must be treated as victims of trafficking. Some escape the compounds only to be detained or prosecuted for immigration offences or crimes committed under threat. No one should be punished for acts they were compelled to carry out because they were trafficked.

From 2022 to 2025, IOM assisted more than 3,500 victims from 39 countries who were trafficked for forced criminality in Southeast Asia. Survivors need protection, medical and psychological care, a safe way home and support to rebuild their lives.

Jobseekers can take precautions. A legitimate employer should have a verifiable address. The contract should describe the work, and the visa should match the job. A recruiter should not pressure someone to travel immediately, keep the offer secret or surrender their passport.

But polished deceptions are designed to appear credible. The burden of defeating sophisticated international criminal networks cannot rest on jobseekers alone.

Before someone boards a flight, there must be a reliable way to verify the offer. When trafficking is suspected, authorities must act together. When a victim escapes, they must be met with protection rather than punishment.

For many people, trafficking now begins with an ordinary message on an ordinary phone. Our response must reach them there.

Every jobseeker should be able to ask: Is this really a job, or is someone trying to lure me into a trap?

None should be left to answer that question alone.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: Head teacher evacuated 900 children minutes before Nepal floods hit
articles.summary: Rajendra Dawadi leapt into action after receiving warnings over waters heading towards his school.
articles.body:
A headteacher has told how he saved 900 pupils' lives from the Nepal floods - by quickly evacuating them just 10 minutes before the waters hit.

Rajendra Dawadi, who is in charge of Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Nuwakot, told the BBC he had received four calls at 09:10 local time (03:25 GMT) warning about the disaster, which has now claimed at least 794 lives.

He quickly decided to evacuate, telling the children to run to higher ground and ordering buses full of students to turn around to flee the area.

Dawadi said: "If we didn't make a quick decision, if it was 10 minutes later, we all - including the students and me - wouldn't be able to speak to you today."

What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods

The warnings had come from four different people in the space of minutes and helped him evaluate the impending danger.

"A parent came and told me that 'a big flood was coming, I am here to take my daughter, I will take her'," he added.

"Parents don't rush without a strong reason, so it was confirmed that I shouldn't waste a second to evacuate the children.

"I decided I shouldn't delay any more. Even if the flood was not coming, it was just a matter of a single day's classes.

"I feel proud that we saved so many lives."

The floods - which decimated parts of Nepal on Wednesday and have left at least 2,426 people missing - saw the school building buried under mud and debris.

Dawadi said the waters arrived so quickly that a hostel building about 100m (328ft) from the river was engulfed immediately.

At first, many students did not realise how serious the situation was.

Pupil Yunisha Amatya, 16, said she scrambled to safety with her friends just before the flood hit.

"I along with my friends survived by just 10 seconds only," she told the BBC.

"Just before the flood came, we were in the class studying. Teachers had gathered in one place and initially had no idea what had happened. After five minutes teachers came and informed us about the flood and asked us to go home."

She said one student fainted after hearing about the disaster, but many initially underestimated the danger and waited for classmates who were in a maths lesson.

Yunisha and her friends scrambled uphill through an escape route behind the school.

"I could not walk fast, and my friends helped me to climb uphill. We tried our best to be in the safer zones then. We escaped through a narrow ladder from backside of the school. Within no time, the bazaar was swept away in front of my eyes," she says, referring to the local market around the school.

"If there was no grip in my shoes I would have fallen and students and other people were jostling each other to reach the safer area while escaping. The people who choose to escape from another route are apparently swept away."

Students and teachers initially moved a few hundred metres uphill to safety before making their way to a neighbouring village.

With roads cut off and transport disrupted, many remained stranded for two nights before rescue efforts reached them.

The principal and Yunisha, who both live across the river from the school, were eventually airlifted back to their home village.

Meanwhile parents were desperately trying to contact their children and relatives.

Yunisha's mother, Sabina Kumari Shrestha, says she repeatedly tried to call both her daughter and husband, but neither could be reached.

Her husband, Yubaraj Amatya, immediately headed towards the school.

"Soon after the flood news spread, I tried my daughter's number, but she was not reachable, then I was afraid," he said.

"Within a few minutes I rushed toward my daughter's school and Trishuli Bazar was all swept by the flood, then I thought my daughter was no more. I was so horrified, stopped my scooter, there was flooding but I could not think of returning without my daughter."

For nearly an hour, he had no idea whether she was alive and kept calling her without success. Then the phone finally connected and Yunisha answered.

"Finally, my daughter received my call and I couldn't stop myself, broke out... two relatives that were with me also cried and hugged me," he said.

Yunisha appears tearful as she recalls that moment.

"After I had reached the top of the hill, I received a call from my father. He was tearful and I could not speak a word then," she said.

Back home, her family waited anxiously for her return.

"Even my younger daughter couldn't sleep. But I felt so good to see her after three days (Friday), I am so happy and relieved," her mother said.

Yunisha says she is now thinking about what comes next.

"Now I am worried about my further studies," she said.

"If I had to change my school, I would have to miss my old friends and will face difficulties to make new friends. I am sad about my further studies."

Head teacher Dawadi says better warning systems, including sirens and evacuation alerts, could have helped residents respond sooner.

But he believes his decision to act immediately prevented a catastrophe.

"Had I decided to close the school after the period, nothing might be left, only the bell would be ringing at 9:30."
authors: Ashok Dahal and Kamal Pariyar, BBC Nepali
